body_markdown:
Spatial Networks, Inc. just earned ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certification, as announced in today’s[press release](https://www.fulcrumapp.com/newsroom/spatial-networks-achieves-iso-27001-certification/) . If the name is new to you, it’s the legal identity of the company you know as Fulcrum. It’s the same company and the same platform, now with an internationally recognized certificate behind the field data you keep there.


An accredited independent auditor examined how Spatial Networks, Inc. builds and runs the Fulcrum platform. The ISO 27001 certification took effect on October 14, 2026, and covers the critical infrastructure in the production environment, where customer data lives, along with the hosted Fulcrum application and the security controls on workstations used to build and maintain the platform. Fulcrum also completes a SOC 2 Type II audit every year, and together the two give customers outside evidence to bring into their own security reviews. Here’s what each one involves and how they fit together.


## What ISO 27001 certification covers


[ISO describes the standard](https://iso.org/standard/27001) as the requirements for building, running, and continually improving an information security management system. In plainer terms, it checks whether a company treats security as an everyday practice with clear owners and documented processes. A company can’t cram for it the night before, because the standard expects ongoing risk assessment and steady improvement, and a surveillance audit every year. The certificate stays valid for three years, as long as each of those annual audits goes well. Each company picks the controls its own risks call for, then shows an auditor that every one of them works.


Reviewers also look closely at who issued a certificate, since an auditor’s credentials decide how much the paper is worth. In the United States, the[ANSI National Accreditation Board (ANAB)](https://blog.ansi.org/anab/iso-iec-27001-2022-information-security-systems/?amp=1) accredits the certification bodies that audit against ISO/IEC 27001. The auditor that certified Spatial Networks, Inc. holds ANAB accreditation, so the firm checking Fulcrum’s security has been through an audit of its own.


## ISO 27001 vs SOC 2: how the two work together


In a SOC 2 audit, an independent accounting firm evaluates Fulcrum’s controls against the[Trust Services Criteria](https://www.aicpa-cima.com/resources/landing/system-and-organization-controls-soc-suite-of-services) from the American Institute of Certified Public Accountants.


SOC 2 reports come in two types. A Type I report checks whether a company’s controls are designed properly on a single date. The more demanding Type II report tests whether those controls worked as intended across a full review period, often several months long.


ISO/IEC 27001 zooms out to the management system running those controls: who owns each risk, how decisions get made, and how the program improves. Side by side, the two show reviewers the machinery of Fulcrum’s security program and a record of how well it ran.


With ISO surveillance audits and the SOC 2 Type II audit each running on an annual schedule, independent auditors check the Spatial Networks security program at least once a year. Reviewers get updated evidence on both fronts with each cycle, so a security assessment never has to lean on findings that went stale years ago.


## How the certificate shortens utility and contractor security reviews


A vendor security assessment at a utility can stretch across weeks of back-and-forth, follow-up calls, and evidence requests. The ISO 27001 certificate settles a large share of those questions in one document, before the first follow-up call. Reviewers can instead spend their time on the questions unique to their own systems, and procurement gets an answer sooner.


Contractors who serve utilities run into the same reviews, since their clients ask about every platform on a project. A certificate from the company behind their field platform hands them a ready answer. It stays valid through October 2029, long enough to outlast most procurement cycles and a few contract renewals.


## Independent proof for the data customers rely on


Field records outlast the projects that produce them, so protecting them is a long-term responsibility. ISO 27001 certification puts an accredited auditor behind the Spatial Networks security program that protects your Fulcrum data, and the annual SOC 2 Type II audit has an accounting firm test its controls on a regular schedule. Together they give customers a program that outside professionals examine every year, with documentation ready for any review that follows.


## **For the IT team running the review**


The[Fulcrum for IT professionals data sheet](https://www.fulcrumapp.com/resources/data-sheet/fulcrum-for-it-professionals/) has the full rundown on security controls, identity management, architecture, and integrations.


The ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certificate of registration issued to Spatial Networks, Inc. is also available through the[Fulcrum Trust Center](https://trust.fulcrumapp.com/) or from your Fulcrum representative.
